28	// handleCommandMode handles a key while the command line owns the keyboard.
29	// Every key first clears the warning on the list's bottom rule: it lasts until
30	// the next keystroke, with no timer.
31	func (a *App) handleCommandMode(msg tea.KeyMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
32		a.sugNotice = ""
33	
34		switch msg.Type {
35		case tea.KeyEsc:
36			return a, a.closeCommandLine()
37		case tea.KeyTab:
38			a.completeHighlighted()
39			return a, nil
40		case tea.KeyShiftTab:
41			return a, nil
42		case tea.KeyUp:
43			a.moveHighlight(-1)
44			return a, nil
45		case tea.KeyDown:
46			a.moveHighlight(1)
47			return a, nil
48		case tea.KeyEnter:
49			return a.runCommand()
50		}
51		return a.handleCommandInput(msg)
52	}
53	
54	// handleCommandInput feeds an ordinary key to the input and ranks the registry
55	// again for the new text.
56	func (a *App) handleCommandInput(msg tea.KeyMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
57		var cmd tea.Cmd
58		before := a.commandInput.Value()
59		a.commandInput, cmd = a.commandInput.Update(msg)
60		if a.commandInput.Value() != before {
61			a.refreshSuggestions()
62		}
63		return a, cmd
64	}
65	
66	// closeCommandLine leaves command mode and asks for the re-layout that gives
67	// the row back to the inactive prompt. The list goes with the line.
68	func (a *App) closeCommandLine() tea.Cmd {
69		a.commandMode = false
70		a.commandInput.Blur()
71		a.resetSuggestions()
72		return a.requestResize()
73	}
74	
75	// runnableText is the single availability question for enter, read by the
76	// header (to grey it) and by runCommand (to refuse). With a list drawn it is
77	// the highlighted row's name. At the argument stage, or with no list drawn
78	// (too short a viewport), it is the text as typed: a prefix such as "co" is
79	// not a name and runs nothing, but an empty line has nothing to run.
80	func (a *App) runnableText() (string, bool) {
81		if a.suggestions.Stage != command.StageArgument && a.listVisible() > 0 {
82			entry, ok := a.highlightedEntry()
83			return entry.Name, ok
84		}
85		input := a.commandInput.Value()
86		return input, strings.TrimSpace(input) != ""
87	}
88	
89	// runCommand executes the highlighted row, or at the argument stage the text
90	// as typed. With nothing to run it says so on the list's bottom rule and
91	// leaves the line open.
92	func (a *App) runCommand() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
93		input, ok := a.runnableText()
94		if !ok {
95			// Only a drawn list has a rule to carry the notice; without one the
96			// refusal is silent, a documented exception to Rule 130.
97			if a.listVisible() > 0 {
98				a.sugNotice = a.nothingToRunNotice()
99			}
100			return a, nil
101		}
102	
103		cmd := command.ParseCommand(input)
104	
105		switch cmd.Type {
106		case command.CommandQuit:
107			a.resetSuggestions()
108			return a, tea.Quit
109	
110		case command.CommandView:
111			a.commandMode = false
112			a.commandInput.Blur()
113			a.resetSuggestions()
114			a.resetSelectionModeFor(cmd.View)
115			return a, a.switchView(cmd.View)
116	
117		case command.CommandContext:
118			a.commandMode = false
119			a.commandInput.Blur()
120			a.resetSuggestions()
121			if len(cmd.Args) > 0 {
122				// Create/switch to a named context
123				return a, a.switchContext(cmd.Args[0])
124			}
125			// No args -> open the interactive modal
126			return a, a.listContexts()
127		}
128	
129		return a, nil
130	}
131	
132	// resetSelectionModeFor takes a view out of selection mode before switching to
133	// it, by dropping it so it is rebuilt normally.
134	//
135	// Only the workspaces view is lent now. The images view was the other one — the
136	// security form borrowed it to pick a scan target — and it could not simply be
137	// dropped, because it holds scan results worth keeping; it took a
138	// ResetSelectionMsg instead. That whole path went with the form (phase 3).
139	//
140	// The security and network views are dropped too, when they are showing what
141	// another view sent them: workspaces and images set the security view's
142	// OriginView, and status's H sets netdiag's. What such a view shows is that
143	// view's detail, not its own state. Naming the view asks for the view — its
144	// inventory, or a blank form — and keeping the detail answered with the same
145	// thing again, with esc leading back to where it came from.
146	//
147	// A view reached by name has no origin and is kept, like every other view's
148	// state across a switch.
149	func (a *App) resetSelectionModeFor(view command.ViewType) {
150		switch view {
151		case command.ViewWorkspaces:
152			delete(a.views, view)
153		case command.ViewFiles:
154			// A picker left behind — the user typed a command instead of choosing —
155			// answers a borrower; the name asks for the browser.
156			if held, ok := a.views[view].(filebrowser.Model); ok && held.Picking() {
157				delete(a.views, view)
158			}
159		case command.ViewSecurity:
160			if held, ok := a.views[view].(security.Model); ok && held.OriginView != "" {
161				delete(a.views, view)
162			}
163		case command.ViewNetdiag:
164			// The same rule, with one precaution the security view does not need: a
165			// diagnostic sent from status may still be walking its stages, and
166			// dropping the view would discard that run without a word. A run in
167			// flight keeps its view; esc on it still returns to status.
168			if held, ok := a.views[view].(*netdiag.Model); ok && held.OriginView != "" && !held.Running() {
169				delete(a.views, view)
170			}
171		}
172	}
173	
174	// switchView changes the current view
175	func (a *App) switchView(view command.ViewType) tea.Cmd {
176		if view != a.currentView {
177			if cmd, ok := a.settleCurrentView(); !ok {
178				return cmd
179			}
180		}
181	
182		// Lazy loading of views
183		if _, exists := a.views[view]; !exists {
184			a.createView(view)
185		}
186	
187		a.currentView = view
188	
189		newView, ok := a.views[view]
190		if !ok {
191			return nil
192		}
193		log.Printf("Switching to view: %s, calling Init()", view)
194	
195		// Init() + a WindowSizeMsg to force the resize, plus the snapshot of
196		// work in progress: the view was kept up to date for as long as it
197		// existed, but a view built just now was not there for anything that had
198		// already started.
199		return tea.Batch(newView.Init(), a.requestResize(), a.sendJobsTo(view))
200	}
201	
202	// settleCurrentView gives the view being left the chance to write down what it
203	// holds, and lets it refuse to be left.
204	//
205	// A view that does not implement LeavingView is left without ceremony, which is
206	// every view but two: the configuration form keeps a value in a widget rather
207	// than in the model until a key moves the cursor, and the agent usage view has a
208	// live poll to stop.
209	//
210	// Returning false keeps the current view *and* whatever it wants to say about
211	// why — the caller passes that Cmd on rather than the switch it did not make.
212	func (a *App) settleCurrentView() (tea.Cmd, bool) {
213		current, exists := a.views[a.currentView]
214		if !exists {
215			return nil, true
216		}
217		leaver, implements := current.(LeavingView)
218		if !implements {
219			return nil, true
220		}
221		settled, cmd, ok := leaver.Leave()
222		a.views[a.currentView] = settled
223		return cmd, ok
224	}
225	
226	// createView creates a view (lazy loading)
227	func (a *App) createView(view command.ViewType) {
228		if _, exists := a.views[view]; exists && view != command.ViewGitAuth {
229			return
230		}
231	
232		switch view {
233		case command.ViewDashboard:
234			a.views[view] = dashboard.New(a.config, a.sharedState)
235		case command.ViewStatus:
236			a.views[view] = status.New(a.config)
237		case command.ViewGitAuth:
238			a.views[view] = a.newAuthView()
239		case command.ViewGitExplorer:
240			a.views[view] = explorer.New(a.config, a.sharedState)
241		case command.ViewWorkspaces:
242			a.views[view] = workspaces.New(a.config, a.sharedState.Secrets.Storage)
243		case command.ViewSecurity:
244			a.views[view] = security.New(a.config, a.sharedState.Secrets.Storage)
245		case command.ViewContainers:
246			a.views[view] = containers.New(a.config)
247		case command.ViewOCIResources:
248			a.views[view] = ociresources.New(a.config)
249		case command.ViewNetdiag:
250			a.views[view] = netdiag.New(a.config)
251		case command.ViewAgentUsage:
252			a.views[view] = agentusageview.New(a.config)
253		case command.ViewConfiguration:
254			a.views[view] = configuration.New(a.config, a.mcpFacts())
255		case command.ViewJobs:
256			a.views[view] = jobsview.New(a.config, a.currentContext)
257		case command.ViewTemplates:
258			a.views[view] = templates.New(a.config, a.sharedState.Secrets.Storage)
259		case command.ViewAbout:
260			a.views[view] = about.New(a.config)
261		case command.ViewFiles:
262			a.views[view] = filebrowser.New(a.config)
263		case command.ViewViewer:
264			// Empty: the viewer is normally installed with its source by
265			// handleViewerOpenRequest, and this case exists so the router can build
266			// one like any other view — which is what the contract test does.
267			a.views[view] = uiviewer.New(a.config)
268		}
269		// Built after the detection landed, it was not there to receive it.
270		a.sendScanToolsTo(view)
271	}
272	
273	// newAuthView builds the GitLab auth view against this context's credentials.
274	// It is rebuilt on every switch rather than cached, so the form reflects the
275	// session that is current now.
276	func (a *App) newAuthView() tea.Model {
277		log.Printf("Creating GitLab auth view with context: %s", a.currentContext)
278	
279		authView := auth.New(a.config, a.sharedState.Secrets, a.sharedState.SecretNotices)
280		if a.sharedState.IsAuthenticated {
281			authView.SetAuth(a.sharedState.Forge, a.sharedState.CurrentUser)
282		}
283		return authView
284	}

40	// LeavingView is implemented by a view that holds an edit the user has not
41	// settled yet, and that would otherwise be lost when the router switches away,
42	// or that has a timer or a read in flight to stop (the :agent-usage poll chain).
43	//
44	// The router had no such point at all: switchView told nobody, so the
45	// configuration view's focused text field was written only by ↑↓ or tab. A path
46	// typed and abandoned with ctrl+p went nowhere, and the cached view kept showing
47	// it (§1.3 D62).
48	//
49	// Leave returns the settled view, whatever the settling has to say, and whether
50	// it may happen. A refusal cancels the switch — the alternative, letting the
51	// user go and reporting the abandoned value in the footer, cannot report
52	// anything: the footer belongs to the view, and the view is what leaves.
53	type LeavingView interface {
54		Leave() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd, bool)
55	}
56	
57	// FilterBarView is implemented by views that have a visible filter bar.
58	// When the filter bar is visible, the viewport bottom border corners are
59	// replaced with T-junction chars (├/┤) to form a closed rectangle.
60	type FilterBarView interface {
61		FilterBarVisible() bool
62	}
63	
64	// App is the main model, with a multi-view router
65	type App struct {
66		config         *config.Config
67		currentContext string
68		viewport       viewport.Model
69	
70		// Navigation
71		currentView command.ViewType
72		views       map[command.ViewType]tea.Model
73		sharedState *shared.State
74	
75		commandMode  bool
76		commandInput textinput.Model
77	
78		// Command suggestions (DEVDESK-89): the list drawn over the viewport while
79		// the command line is open.
80		suggester   *command.Suggester
81		suggestions command.Suggestions

69	  registry — name, aliases, description, argument placeholder, kind. The parser,
70	  the listings and the suggestions all derive from it.

72	  input: exact name or alias, then name prefix, then alias prefix. Once the first
73	  word names a command that takes an argument and a space follows, it switches to
74	  the argument stage (`Suggestions.Stage`) with that single entry.

76	  whole lines, never a cut of styled text, with a bottom rule carrying the count
77	  (`3 of 17`, `▲ n more · ▼ m more`) or the warning. `VisibleRows` caps it at
78	  eight rows and at the usable viewport height minus the rule; below two usable
79	  lines there is no list.

81	  highlighted row (`sugCursor`, -1 for none), the scroll offset and the notice;
82	  `renderBody` swaps the viewport's top lines for the list (`FrameJoined` ├─┤, or
83	  `FrameClosed` └─┘ for a frameless view such as the dashboard).

86	move the highlight without wrapping (from no highlight, `↓` takes the first
87	visible row and `↑` the last); `tab` writes the highlighted name into the line,
88	plus a space when it takes an argument, and runs nothing; `enter` opens the
89	highlighted row, or at the argument stage runs the text as typed (`ctx work`
90	creates or switches); `esc` closes the line and the list together. `shift+tab` does
91	nothing. With nothing highlighted `tab` and `enter` are greyed in the header
92	(`commandLineShortcuts`, which replaces the view's own shortcuts), and `enter`
93	says why on the bottom rule: `Type a name or choose one` for an empty line (it

96	`enter` runs the text as typed, like the argument stage: `containers` opens the
97	view, `co` runs nothing and the line stays open (no notice, there is no rule to
98	carry it). `View` is cut to the terminal's height by `fitHeight` (`view.go`):
99	the surplus comes off the bottom of the viewport first, so the header's command

443	- `ctx wrok` (aucun résultat) : ligne `No context starts with "wrok"` ; `enter` n'est **pas** modifié ici (la création implicite et ses messages relèvent de `context-switch.md` §3-5).
444	- Chargement : la liste des contextes est lue par une `Cmd` (règle 110), jamais dans `View()`. Tant qu'elle n'est pas arrivée : une ligne `Loading contexts…` et `enter` n'agit pas. On n'affiche **pas** « No context » avant d'avoir la réponse (principe de la règle 130 : ne pas savoir n'est pas savoir que c'est non).
445	- Extension : le moteur de suggestions prend un « fournisseur » par commande (vues : statique ; `context` : contextes). Les mots réservés `-`, `new` de `context-switch.md` s'insèrent après les contextes, sans changer la grille.
446	
447	## 9. Impact pour les autres rôles
448	
449	**À faire quoi qu'on choisisse (défauts, pas du design)** — à porter au `pm` comme `bug` :

55	- `jobs` or `j` - Switch to the jobs view: what is running, and what ran this session
56	- `agent-usage` or `au` - Switch to the agent usage view: Claude Code sessions found on disk, by project and date
57	- `templates` or `tpl` - Switch to the repository template catalog (see [templates.md](templates.md))
58	- `files` or `fs` - Browse the whole filesystem: create and delete files and directories; also the picker a form's path field opens with enter (see [filebrowser.md](filebrowser.md))
59	- `about` or `version` - Which build is running: version, commit, build date, and where the config, cache and log live
60	- `context <name>` or `ctx <name>` - Switch configuration context
61	- `context list` - Show available contexts
62	- `quit` - Exit application
63	
64	**The command line shows a suggestion list (DEVDESK-89).** Opening it (`ctrl+p`
65	or `:`) draws a list of every view and action over the top of the viewport; each
66	keystroke ranks it again. The pieces:
67	
68	- `command.Entries()` (`internal/command/registry.go`) is the one ordered
69	  registry — name, aliases, description, argument placeholder, kind. The parser,
70	  the listings and the suggestions all derive from it.
71	- `command.Suggester` (`internal/command/suggest.go`) ranks the registry for the
72	  input: exact name or alias, then name prefix, then alias prefix. Once the first
73	  word names a command that takes an argument and a space follows, it switches to
74	  the argument stage (`Suggestions.Stage`) with that single entry.
75	- `internal/ui/cmdsuggest` renders the list as pure lines (state in, lines out):
76	  whole lines, never a cut of styled text, with a bottom rule carrying the count
77	  (`3 of 17`, `▲ n more · ▼ m more`) or the warning. `VisibleRows` caps it at
78	  eight rows and at the usable viewport height minus the rule; below two usable
79	  lines there is no list.
80	- The router (`internal/app/command_suggestions.go`) holds the result, the
81	  highlighted row (`sugCursor`, -1 for none), the scroll offset and the notice;
82	  `renderBody` swaps the viewport's top lines for the list (`FrameJoined` ├─┤, or
83	  `FrameClosed` └─┘ for a frameless view such as the dashboard).
84	
85	Keys in the command line: typing ranks again and highlights the best row; `↑`/`↓`
86	move the highlight without wrapping (from no highlight, `↓` takes the first
87	visible row and `↑` the last); `tab` writes the highlighted name into the line,
88	plus a space when it takes an argument, and runs nothing; `enter` opens the
89	highlighted row, or at the argument stage runs the text as typed (`ctx work`
90	creates or switches); `esc` closes the line and the list together. `shift+tab` does
91	nothing. With nothing highlighted `tab` and `enter` are greyed in the header
92	(`commandLineShortcuts`, which replaces the view's own shortcuts), and `enter`
93	says why on the bottom rule: `Type a name or choose one` for an empty line (it
94	never quits and changes nothing), `"zz" is not a view or a command` for no match.
95	With no list drawn (viewport below two usable lines) nothing is highlighted and
96	`enter` runs the text as typed, like the argument stage: `containers` opens the
97	view, `co` runs nothing and the line stays open (no notice, there is no rule to
98	carry it). `View` is cut to the terminal's height by `fitHeight` (`view.go`):
99	the surplus comes off the bottom of the viewport first, so the header's command
100	line and the footer outrank viewport rows; no change at normal heights.
101	Its floor: below 9 lines the command line itself (the header's 9th line) is cut,
102	and at 13 lines or fewer the FilterBar's top edge can disappear with the viewport.
103	`enter` is greyed or lit by `runnableText` (`command_line.go`), the one function
104	`commandLineShortcuts` and `runCommand` both read. **Declared exception to Rule
105	130:** with no list drawn (unknown name, empty line, terminal under 14 lines) a
106	refused `enter` is silent, there being no rule to carry the notice.
107	The notice lasts until the next key, with no timer. The ghost completion text and
108	the `[i/n]` position that used to follow the input, and the breadcrumb of views
109	`tab` used to open, are gone. `tab` here is a declared exception to Rule 135
110	(`keymap.DeclaredExceptions()`, surface `app/command-line`).
111	
112	Command parsing lives in `internal/command/`. `ParseCommand()` returns a structured `Command{Type, View, Args}` supporting `CommandView`, `CommandContext`, `CommandQuit`, `CommandUnknown`.
113	
114	**The forge views are `git-auth` and `git-explorer`, named after the role.**

95	// footerMsgSeq numbers messages so a timer can name the one it was started for.
96	var footerMsgSeq atomic.Uint64
97	
98	// ClearFooterMsg expires the message identified by ID.
99	//
100	// The ID is what makes the type safe to share across packages. Two things would
101	// otherwise go wrong: a timer started by one view could clear the message of
102	// whichever view is active when it lands, and — the bug that was already
103	// present in all eight local implementations — a message set at t+2.9s was
104	// wiped at t+3s by its predecessor's timer.
105	type ClearFooterMsg struct{ ID uint64 }
106	
107	// PostFooterMsg puts a message in whichever footer is on screen.
108	//
109	// It exists for the router, which has none of its own: RenderFooter is the
110	// active view's (internal/app/view.go), and the one thing the router has to say
111	// — that the MCP server did not start (§3.61) — belongs on screen at startup,
112	// not in a log. Every view already offers unhandled messages to Handle, so a
113	// broadcast lands wherever the user is without any view knowing what it is
114	// about.
115	//
116	// It carries its own ID because the timer is the sender's: PostFooter builds
117	// both, so the rule that a message set without its timer never clears holds
118	// here too (Rule 128).
119	//
120	// **It lands only where a view holds a FooterMessage.** internal/ui/forge/auth
121	// renders a footer but declares none, so a broadcast posted while that view is
122	// on screen reaches nobody — and the router switches to it whenever a context
123	// has no forge credentials. That is a real gap and not a silent one: the only
124	// broadcast today is the MCP server's, and its state is also on the `mcp` tab
125	// of the configuration view, which holds it for as long as it is true rather
126	// than for three seconds. A second use of this door would need auth to declare
127	// a footer first.
128	type PostFooterMsg struct {
129		ID    uint64
130		Level Level
131		Text  string
132	}
133	
134	// PostFooter builds the broadcast and the timer that expires it.
135	//
136	// For the router. A view has its own footer and calls Info, Warn or Error on
137	// it — going through here would be a second way to do what a field already
138	// does, and the message would be adopted by whatever view is active rather than
139	// by the one that meant it.
140	func PostFooter(level Level, text string) tea.Cmd {
141		if text == "" {
142			return nil
143		}
144		id := footerMsgSeq.Add(1)
145		return tea.Batch(
146			func() tea.Msg { return PostFooterMsg{ID: id, Level: level, Text: text} },
147			tea.Tick(FooterMsgDuration, func(time.Time) tea.Msg { return ClearFooterMsg{ID: id} }),
148		)
149	}
150	
151	// FooterMessage holds the current message, its level and its identity.
152	type FooterMessage struct {
153		text         string
154		level        Level
155		id           uint64
156		spinnerFrame string
157	}
158	
159	// Info, Warn and Error set the message and return its expiry timer. Call them
160	// from Update() and return the Cmd — a message set without its timer never
161	// clears (Rule 128).
162	func (f *FooterMessage) Info(text string) tea.Cmd  { return f.set(text, LevelInfo) }
163	func (f *FooterMessage) Warn(text string) tea.Cmd  { return f.set(text, LevelWarning) }
164	func (f *FooterMessage) Error(text string) tea.Cmd { return f.set(text, LevelError) }
165	
166	func (f *FooterMessage) set(text string, level Level) tea.Cmd {
167		if text == "" {
168			f.Clear()
169			return nil
170		}
171		f.text = text
172		f.level = level
173		f.id = footerMsgSeq.Add(1)
174	
175		id := f.id
176		return tea.Tick(FooterMsgDuration, func(time.Time) tea.Msg {
177			return ClearFooterMsg{ID: id}
178		})
179	}
180	
181	// Clear removes the message now, without waiting for its timer.
182	func (f *FooterMessage) Clear() {
183		f.text = ""
184		f.level = LevelInfo

95	// footerMsgSeq numbers messages so a timer can name the one it was started for.
96	var footerMsgSeq atomic.Uint64
97	
98	// ClearFooterMsg expires the message identified by ID.
99	//
100	// The ID is what makes the type safe to share across packages. Two things would
101	// otherwise go wrong: a timer started by one view could clear the message of
102	// whichever view is active when it lands, and — the bug that was already
103	// present in all eight local implementations — a message set at t+2.9s was
104	// wiped at t+3s by its predecessor's timer.
105	type ClearFooterMsg struct{ ID uint64 }
106	
107	// PostFooterMsg puts a message in whichever footer is on screen.
108	//
109	// It exists for the router, which has none of its own: RenderFooter is the
110	// active view's (internal/app/view.go), and the one thing the router has to say
111	// — that the MCP server did not start (§3.61) — belongs on screen at startup,
112	// not in a log. Every view already offers unhandled messages to Handle, so a
113	// broadcast lands wherever the user is without any view knowing what it is
114	// about.
115	//
116	// It carries its own ID because the timer is the sender's: PostFooter builds
117	// both, so the rule that a message set without its timer never clears holds
118	// here too (Rule 128).
119	//
120	// **It lands only where a view holds a FooterMessage.** internal/ui/forge/auth
121	// renders a footer but declares none, so a broadcast posted while that view is
122	// on screen reaches nobody — and the router switches to it whenever a context
123	// has no forge credentials. That is a real gap and not a silent one: the only
124	// broadcast today is the MCP server's, and its state is also on the `mcp` tab
125	// of the configuration view, which holds it for as long as it is true rather
126	// than for three seconds. A second use of this door would need auth to declare
127	// a footer first.
128	type PostFooterMsg struct {
129		ID    uint64
130		Level Level
131		Text  string
132	}
133	
134	// PostFooter builds the broadcast and the timer that expires it.
135	//
136	// For the router. A view has its own footer and calls Info, Warn or Error on
137	// it — going through here would be a second way to do what a field already
138	// does, and the message would be adopted by whatever view is active rather than
139	// by the one that meant it.
140	func PostFooter(level Level, text string) tea.Cmd {
141		if text == "" {
142			return nil
143		}
144		id := footerMsgSeq.Add(1)
145		return tea.Batch(
146			func() tea.Msg { return PostFooterMsg{ID: id, Level: level, Text: text} },
147			tea.Tick(FooterMsgDuration, func(time.Time) tea.Msg { return ClearFooterMsg{ID: id} }),
148		)
149	}
150	
151	// FooterMessage holds the current message, its level and its identity.
152	type FooterMessage struct {
153		text         string
154		level        Level
155		id           uint64
156		spinnerFrame string
157	}
158	
159	// Info, Warn and Error set the message and return its expiry timer. Call them
160	// from Update() and return the Cmd — a message set without its timer never
161	// clears (Rule 128).
162	func (f *FooterMessage) Info(text string) tea.Cmd  { return f.set(text, LevelInfo) }
163	func (f *FooterMessage) Warn(text string) tea.Cmd  { return f.set(text, LevelWarning) }
164	func (f *FooterMessage) Error(text string) tea.Cmd { return f.set(text, LevelError) }
165	
166	func (f *FooterMessage) set(text string, level Level) tea.Cmd {
167		if text == "" {
168			f.Clear()
169			return nil
170		}
171		f.text = text
172		f.level = level

174	
175		id := f.id
176		return tea.Tick(FooterMsgDuration, func(time.Time) tea.Msg {
177			return ClearFooterMsg{ID: id}
178		})
179	}

## DEVDESK-88 : plan d'architecture (`:ctx` : complétion, `ctx -`, `ctx new`)

**Ce que dit le code.** Une partie de l'infrastructure existe déjà mais rien ne s'en sert. `command.ArgProvider`, `Suggester.WithProvider`, `Suggestions.Args` et `ArgsReady` sont dans `internal/command/suggest.go`, sans aucun appelant, et `cmdsuggest.Render` n'affiche pas les `Args`. Le routeur n'a pas de `FooterMessage` : il parle avec `components.PostFooter`, un message diffusé à la vue active, déjà utilisé par mcp.go et forward.go.
Quatre pièges :
1. `ParseCommand` met toute la saisie en minuscules, donc `ctx Work` devient `work` et l'erreur E4 ne peut jamais apparaître.
2. Un nouveau contexte n'a pas de forge, donc on atterrit sur `ViewGitAuth`. C'est la seule vue sans `FooterMessage` : le message E8 serait perdu.
3. `ctx list` crée aujourd'hui un contexte nommé « list », alors que la doc le décrit comme « List available contexts ».
4. Il ne faut pas modifier `ValidateContextName` : `LoadContext` et `SetCurrentContext` l'appellent, et un contexte existant nommé `new` deviendrait illisible.

**Options.** Pour les messages : (A) `PostFooter` avec un `FooterMessage` ajouté à la vue auth, ou (B) un `FooterMessage` porté par le routeur qui remplace la ligne d'info de la vue. Je recommande **A** : c'est le mécanisme déjà prévu et la mise en page ne change pas. Pour la complétion : brancher l'`ArgProvider` existant, plutôt qu'un moteur parallèle qui ferait doublon.

**Étapes** (TDD ; le tester écrit d'abord les tests indiqués)
1. **config : noms réservés et erreurs typées** (`internal/config/config.go`, `context_test.go`, `internal/ui/setup/model.go:459`).
   - À créer : `ErrReservedContextName`, `ErrContextExists`, `ErrContextNotFound`, et `ValidateNewContextName(name string) error` (format, puis refus de `-`, `new`, `list`). `CreateContext` l'utilise et enveloppe `ErrContextExists`.
   - Tests : `CreateContext("new")` donne `errors.Is` Reserved et aucun fichier ; un contexte existant donne `ErrContextExists` ; `LoadContext("list")` sur un fichier existant fonctionne toujours. Commande : `go test ./internal/config ./internal/ui/setup`.
2. **Le parseur garde la casse de l'argument** (`internal/command/parser.go`) : seul le premier mot est normalisé.
   - Tests : `":CTX Work"` donne `{CommandContext, ["Work"]}` ; `"Status"` ouvre toujours la vue status. Commande : `go test ./internal/command`.
3. **Résolveur pur `internal/contextcmd`**, nouveau paquet sans I/O.
   - Signatures : `type Snapshot{Names []string; Current, Previous string; Ready bool}` ; `Resolve(args []string, highlighted string, s Snapshot) Action` avec `Action{Kind (List|Switch|Create|Refuse|KeepOpen); Name; Level; Text}` ; `Match(prefix string, names []string) []string` (préfixe insensible à la casse, correspondance exacte en tête) ; `DidYouMean(name string, names []string) (string, bool)` (Levenshtein ≤ 2 ou préfixe commun ≥ 3).
   - Messages E1 à E9 en constantes ou fonctions nommées.
   - Tests : table couvrant chaque branche de l'arbre de décision du §3.5 de `docs/ux/context-switch.md`, avec les libellés exacts. Commande : `go test ./internal/contextcmd`.
4. **Fournisseur d'arguments et instantané** (`internal/app/context_args.go`, `app.go`).
   - `contextArgs.SuggestArgs(prefix)` lit seulement l'instantané, donc rien dans `View()` ; il rend `(nil, false)` tant que la liste n'est pas chargée.
   - Ordre : contextes, puis `-` et `new`, filtrés par préfixe ; après `new ` : aucune ligne.
   - `newWithSize` enregistre le fournisseur avec `WithProvider("context", …)`. `enterCommandMode` lance aussi `loadContextNamesCmd()`, qui produit `contextNamesLoadedMsg{Names, Err}`.
   - Tests : avec `isolateHome` et 2 fichiers de contexte, l'ouverture de la ligne produit le message, et le fournisseur rend la liste attendue. Dépend de 3.
5. **Rendu des arguments** (`internal/ui/cmdsuggest`).
   - `Input` reçoit `Heading`, `Empty` et `Loading`. Le routeur fabrique des `Row` à partir des `Args` (`Current` = contexte courant).
   - Tests : filet `Contexts · 2 of 5`, ligne `work (current)`, `Loading contexts…`, `No context starts with "wrok"`, chaque ligne fait exactement la largeur, et le test de contraste passe. Parallélisable.
6. **Routeur : étape argument** (`command_suggestions.go`, `command_line.go`).
   - Le nombre de lignes devient celui des lignes d'argument.

**Ce que dit le code.** Une partie de l'infrastructure existe déjà mais rien ne s'en sert. `command.ArgProvider`, `Suggester.WithProvider`, `Suggestions.Args` et `ArgsReady` sont dans `internal/command/suggest.go`, sans aucun appelant, et `cmdsuggest.Render` n'affiche pas les `Args`. Le routeur n'a pas de `FooterMessage` : il parle avec `components.PostFooter`, un message diffusé à la vue active, déjà utilisé par mcp.go et forward.go.
Quatre pièges :
1. `ParseCommand` met toute la saisie en minuscules, donc `ctx Work` devient `work` et l'erreur E4 ne peut jamais apparaître.
2. Un nouveau contexte n'a pas de forge, donc on atterrit sur `ViewGitAuth`. C'est la seule vue sans `FooterMessage` : le message E8 serait perdu.
3. `ctx list` crée aujourd'hui un contexte nommé « list », alors que la doc le décrit comme « List available contexts ».
4. Il ne faut pas modifier `ValidateContextName` : `LoadContext` et `SetCurrentContext` l'appellent, et un contexte existant nommé `new` deviendrait illisible.

**Options.** Pour les messages : (A) `PostFooter` avec un `FooterMessage` ajouté à la vue auth, ou (B) un `FooterMessage` porté par le routeur qui remplace la ligne d'info de la vue.
